metadata.description: Claude Code plugins and skills maintained by Gep

plugins.name: destructive-guard
plugins.description: PreToolUse approval gate with two classifiers, configured through env variables. Sends each Bash and MCP call (redacted) to Clef (typically served locally) and, when Clef cannot answer, to Jev, and asks before risky ones; asks with a warning when neither answers; never allows. With no usable classifier the session halts: Bash and MCP calls are denied and prompts are blocked until a setting is fixed or GATE_ENABLED=0. Blocks .env file access. A session warning names misconfigured settings. Includes a check skill and a Lean model of the gate. Needs Python >= 3.14.

plugins.name: gated-dev-simple-workflow
plugins.description: Ticket-to-PR pipeline for ticket files or Jira issues: /ticket runs spec, plan, dev and review subagents in a worktree per ticket (git, Orca or iTerm2), in heavy, medium or light mode (light skips spec and review for small changes), with the plan split into small dev tasks, each built by its own dev subagent in turn, in three tiers (godzilla, workhorse, pawn) chosen per task and promoted when a tier is too low, with a plan-approval checkpoint and PR creation, then watches the PR: addresses review feedback (--address-review) and cleans up after the merge. Projects can add their own steps at fixed events (for example to sync an issue tracker). Includes a launcher that opens one session per ticket and notifies you when a launched session needs you. Treats approval-gate prompts as checkpoints; no gate required. With a Jira tracker it moves the issue To Do → In Progress → In Review → Done and posts progress comments, using the session's Jira tools. /ticket-flow runs the subtasks of one Jira parent through /ticket, picking the next ready one as slots free. Needs Python >= 3.14.
